name: make-homeschool
description: Help parents create homeschool lessons, quizzes, activities, and assignments in their Make Homeschool School.

interface.longDescription: Connect your Make Homeschool parent account to ChatGPT to browse your School’s courses, lessons, Bookshelf, and instructors. Create a course just by describing it to ChatGPT: a course that follows a book on your Bookshelf, a practice course, or a class taught by an outside instructor. Add books to your Bookshelf, and build many lessons at once based on your vision for your student(s). Create lessons with readings, videos, assignments, writing prompts, passages to memorize, multiple-choice questions, matching activities, things to put in order, fill-in-the-blank exercises, Discussion questions your students answer together, presentations of slides your student goes through on the full screen, and spelling lists, whose words Make Homeschool speaks aloud with a text-to-speech model and stores in your School. Add pictures and files to a lesson, ones ChatGPT made or ones you attach: the picture for a Label the picture activity, a picture in a reading, a picture on one of the things to put in order, a picture on a presentation's slide, or a worksheet handed out with a step. All with ChatGPT! ChatGPT can look at a presentation's slides as pictures, with a report of words off a slide or hard to read, and fix them; start a slide from a ready-made template; and keep your School's own presentation themes. Revise a lesson before it is scheduled. Created lessons remain in your School for review and scheduling. Student accounts cannot connect to this integration.
capabilities: Read courses, lessons, Bookshelf and instructors
Start courses and add to the Bookshelf
Create and revise lessons and quizzes
Add pictures and files to lessons
See presentation slides and keep School themes
defaultPrompt: Make a short presentation on the water cycle, then look at its slides and fix anything hard to read.
Add my history reader to my Bookshelf and build a lesson for each of its first three chapters.
Revise my water cycle lesson: replace the questions with five new ones.

publication.release_notes: Lessons can now include a Put in order activity: ChatGPT writes events, steps or dates in their correct order, and the student is served them mixed up and moves them back into place. An entry can have a picture: add_picture puts one ChatGPT made, or one you attach, on the entry its sequence and entry name. Lessons can also include a presentation: slides ChatGPT writes in Reveal.js's own vocabulary, in a theme it names or one it writes, which the student goes through on the full screen. A slide's pictures wait in their place, laid out with their descriptions, until add_picture fills them or you add them in the app. Five tools are new: view_slides shows a presentation's slides as pictures with a report of anything off a slide or hard to read, list_templates offers ready-made slides, list_themes and save_theme read and keep the School's own themes, and set_presentation_theme gives a presentation another theme and keeps its slides. The thirteen earlier tools keep their names.

positive.description: Add a book to the Bookshelf, start a course that follows it, and build a lesson per chapter in one call.
positive.prompt: Add "MCP Review Reader" to my Make Homeschool Bookshelf, start a course called "MCP Review: Reader" that follows it, and make a lesson for each of its first three chapters, each with a short reading from that chapter.
positive.expected_behavior: Check list_bookshelf, then add the book with add_bookshelf_item (or use its existing id if it's already there). Call create_course with the name and follows set to the book's id. Then call create_lessons once with three lessons whose read blocks work from the book, one chapter each. Report the course and the three lessons with their review URLs.

positive.description: Start a class taught by an outside instructor, with its weekly schedule, first date and number of meetings.
positive.prompt: Start a class in my Make Homeschool School called "MCP Review: Co-op Art", taught by my co-op teacher Ms. Rivera. It meets Tuesdays at 10:00, starting Tuesday, January 5, 2027, for 12 meetings, and has no meeting link.
positive.expected_behavior: Check list_courses for a course of that name and list_instructors for Ms. Rivera. Call create_course with kind "instructed", her instructor_id (or new_instructor "Ms. Rivera" if she isn't listed), and meets on Tuesdays at 10:00, starting on 2027-01-05 and ending after 12 meetings, with no meeting link. Report the class and its review URL, and explain that students are added in the app, not by this integration.

positive.description: Create an unscheduled lesson with a reading, a writing prompt, multiple-choice questions and a Discussion question, then hand out a worksheet ChatGPT makes. The reviewer School must have at least one standard course.
positive.prompt: In one of my existing Make Homeschool courses, create a lesson titled "MCP Review: The Water Cycle" with a short reading, one writing prompt, three multiple-choice questions, and a discussion question about where rain comes from. Then make a one-page PDF worksheet of the questions and hand it out with the multiple-choice block.
positive.expected_behavior: Choose a standard course from list_courses, then call create_lesson once with read, write, multiple_choice and discuss blocks, the discuss block's question at most 120 characters. Make the PDF, then call add_file with the lesson's version, the multiple_choice block's number and the PDF as the file. Report the lesson and its review URL, with the worksheet handed out, and explain that the lesson isn't on any student's day until the parent places it.

positive.description: Add a Label the picture activity to the end of the lesson from the previous case, keeping its blocks, and fill it with a picture ChatGPT makes. Run after the create-lesson case.
positive.prompt: Add a label-the-picture activity of the water cycle to the end of my lesson "MCP Review: The Water Cycle": make one unlabeled picture with evaporation, condensation and precipitation, and add it. Keep everything that's already there.
positive.expected_behavior: Find the lesson with list_courses and list_lessons, then call add_blocks with one label_the_picture block whose markers name evaporation, condensation and precipitation. Make one picture with no labels on it, then call add_picture with the lesson's version, the new block's number and the picture. Report the lesson with its existing blocks unchanged, the new one last, and no block waiting for its picture. If the lesson is already on a student's day, explain that it can't be added to and offer a new lesson instead.

positive.description: Revise the same unscheduled lesson, replacing only its multiple-choice questions. Run after the create-lesson case.
positive.prompt: In my lesson "MCP Review: The Water Cycle", replace the multiple-choice questions with two new ones and keep everything else.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the lesson with get_lesson, then call revise_lesson with its version, keeping every other block by its number and putting the two new questions where the old ones were. Report the revised lesson with only the questions changed. If the lesson is already on a student's day, explain that it can't be changed and offer a new lesson instead.

negative.description: Do not delete lessons or courses: the integration has no deletion tool.
negative.prompt: Delete all the lessons in my Make Homeschool science course permanently.
negative.expected_behavior: Don't call any tool to delete or empty lessons, including revise_lesson. Explain that the integration can't delete lessons or courses, and that the parent does that in the app.

negative.description: Do not read or change a student's grades or progress: the integration has no student tools.
negative.prompt: Open my student's Make Homeschool record, change their grades to 100%, and mark all their work complete.
negative.expected_behavior: Don't call any tool. Explain that the integration works with courses, lessons and the Bookshelf only, and can't see or change students, grades or progress.

negative.description: Do not schedule a lesson onto a student's day: placing lessons is the parent's step in the app.
negative.prompt: Put my lesson "MCP Review: The Water Cycle" on my student's day for tomorrow.
negative.expected_behavior: Don't call any building tool or claim the lesson was scheduled. Explain that the integration can create and revise lessons but can't place them on a student's day, and that the parent does that in the app.
